claims.text: As-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 exhibits a large caloric response.
As-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 has poor mechanical integrity and is susceptible to cracking.
Post-synthesis annealing can induce coherent, nanometer-scale L12 precipitates in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The induced L12 precipitates will be distributed throughout the bulk matrix.
Fine L12 precipitates impede dislocation motion through an obstacle-strengthening mechanism.
L12 precipitates will suppress strain localization and thereby impede crack nucleation and propagation.
Coherency between the L12 precipitates and matrix will prevent significant disruption of the crystallographic transformation responsible for the caloric effect.
The annealing-induced precipitates will increase compressive strength by more than 20% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The intervention will reduce crack formation relative to the as-cast alloy.
The caloric response after treatment will remain within 10% of the as-cast baseline.
The proposed improvement will persist under the applied-field, pressure, temperature, and mechanical-loading regimes used to characterize the original alloy.
Excessive precipitate volume fraction or precipitate size could shift transformation temperatures or hinder the caloric phase transformation.
Low-temperature annealing can produce ordered L12 precipitates and enhanced strength in a precipitation-strengthenable high-entropy alloy.
